title: Digel Cloud 2S
caption: The star-forming region Digel Cloud 2S, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: [YKT2006b] Cloud2-S · constellation Cassiopeia · about 40000 light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, M. Ressler (NASA-JPL)

recognition.text: Ranked #58 on ESA/Webb’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: A compact cluster of luminous red, blue and white stars sits at the center, with faint, clumpy jets reaching out in several directions and a smaller cluster above and to the right. Translucent red wisps stretch across the scene. This is Digel Cloud 2S, a star-forming region in the Extreme Outer Galaxy, seen by Webb.

That region lies at the very outskirts of the Milky Way, over 58 000 light-years out from the center of the Galaxy. To learn how a local environment affects star formation, scientists aimed Webb's NIRCam and MIRI at four star-forming areas in Digel Clouds 1 and 2, labeled 1A, 1B, 2N and 2S.

In Cloud 2S, Webb revealed a bright main cluster of newly formed stars, several of them shooting jets from their poles. The sub-cluster to its upper right had been suspected before and is now confirmed. Winds and radiation from nearby stars are carving away the red nebulous structures.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (1.77 x 1.30 arcminutes) and distance (40000 light years), the frame spans roughly 21 × 15 light-years. Its light set out about 40,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Webb's NIRCam and MIRI combined near- and mid-infrared light. Blue and cyan show the shortest wavelengths, green and yellow intermediate ones, and orange and red the longest, including PAH dust emission.
understand.eye: This infrared light is invisible to the human eye.

explore: Beyond the cloud lies a deep sea of background galaxies, appearing as small blue-white and orange-white dots and thin fuzzy discs. The larger blue-white point with diffraction spikes at upper right is a foreground star.
alt: A compact cluster of red, blue and white stars with faint jets, a smaller cluster to the upper right, red wisps across the scene and scattered background galaxies.
